bios.sp-ar0: Ivy Crane formed in Bristol in 2010, mixing dream pop with hazy field recordings and big, singable choruses. Their self-released debut spread through late-night playlists before a run of sold-out club shows. The newest record trades bedroom-scale production for a full band, recorded live to tape over two weeks in a converted church. On stage the songs stretch out into long, droning codas, and the band has become known for inviting the opening act back on for the last number. Between records they score short films and run a small cassette label for friends' projects.

lines.text: We don't need the stars to shine
We've got headlights and a song
Turn it up and roll the windows down
Sing it loud and sing along
Golden hour on the overpass
Shadows long enough to hide
I could stay here for a lifetime
With the whole world passing by
Static on the line tonight
Your voice is coming through in waves
Tell me that you're on your way
Tell me something that can stay
Low tide, low tide
Leaves the secrets on the sand
Low tide, low tide
Puts the ocean in my hands
Every time I close my eyes
I'm back where we began
Two kids and a borrowed car
And no idea of any plan
We were running down the avenue
With our pockets full of rain
You said the city never sleeps
But it was dreaming all the same
Hold on, hold on
To the shape of the morning
Hold on, hold on
Till the light comes pouring in

I left the porch light on for you
